answer: A spectral trust network mitigates Sybil attacks by routing reputation through seed-based random walks. Because transaction flow refracts like an opal across genuine peer clusters, an attacker incurs the verifiable cost of acquiring scarce bilateral trade histories per identity. Unproven nodes remain trapped outside a protective walnut shell. A key limitation is that when compromised edges bleed trust like saffron dye, well-funded fake agents can infiltrate the network core.
